text: The Patriots pulled off a crucial 29-26 Week 4 upset over the Bills at Highmark Stadium, with Drake Maye rebounding from an early-season slide to deliver a clutch performance that Mike Vrabel characterized as critical for the defending AFC East champions—a stunning comeback that helped New England salvage what looked like a potential 1-3 start and climb to 2-2 alongside fellow rallying teams like the Rams and Cowboys. Off the field, the team made a pair of roster moves, releasing linebacker Jose Ramirez while signing cornerback Al'Zillion Hamilton to the practice squad and cutting offensive lineman Da'Metrius Weatherspoon from it, while also preparing to honor legendary kicker Adam Vinatieri during a halftime ceremony on October 11 against the Raiders, the same team that presents a formidable challenge with tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer looming after the Patriots held down Dalton Kincaid a week prior. Meanwhile, high school football got its moment in the spotlight when Central Catholic Raiders head coach John Dubzinski earned the Patriots Coach of the Week award following his team's 52-51 upset over Xaverian Brothers.
